rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so the pipeline tolerates this program and the weights can be shifted toward stronger obfuscation: all seven passes are enabled with elevated SecurityGain/DiversityGain and lowered cost/risk weights to invite broader application across the 37 small C++ functions. FLA gets the highest security weight since control-flow flattening is the strongest single deterrent for the constructors/destructor hotspots, and its RuntimeCost stays moderate (0.5) because this benchmark's hot loops are short; SUB and BCF are pushed high too since bogus-arithmetic and opaque predicates compound well on top of flattening. SPLIT keeps high DiversityGain but low costs because it is cheap and increases the surface other passes transform; IBR, ICALL, and IGV get mid-high security weights to break basic-block traceability, indirect-call analysis, and global-value identity, with CorrectnessRisk kept at or below 0.3 everywhere so the correctness check that passed in round 1 remains protected while still allowing noticeably more aggressive transformation than the first candidate.
